AUTHOR: Sobolev
TITLE: Convolution Neural Network for Identification of Underwater Objects
VENUE: 2022 Conference of Russian Young Researchers in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ElConRus)
REGION: Sea of Azov near Berdyansk (Black Sea / Sea of Azov), Russia/Ukraine
SPECIES: Liza haematocheilus (adult, juvenile), Neogobius, Syngnathidae, plus jellyfish
DATA: Own field video recorded with a video camera in the Sea of Azov; frames extracted every 30 s, labelled in LabelImg
V_EV: Sec. III.C: 'Due to the complicated environmental properties of the water environment, objects located at the distance doesn't looks clear.'
R_EV: Sec. III.C: 'we test our model on generated video stream in same environmental conditions.'
E_EV: Sec. III.B: 'final overall accuracy reached acceptable level of 72.22%' (only mAP/per-class accuracy reported)
NOTE: Platform not described (stationary camera implied by fish feeding at fixed location). Sea of Azov coded 하구/기수 as brackish sea. Train/test split never described; 259 images in final experiment (24580 after augmentation in exp 1). Qualitative real-time test on video 'in same environmental conditions'. V_ALL=P rests only on a qualitative remark about distant objects; verifier may prefer NR.
AUTHORS_FULL: A. S. Sobolev; S. G. Chernyi; D. O. Krivoguz; A. P. Nyrkov; E. G. Zinchenko
